title: Fancy a cuppa?
description: Would you like some tea?
details:
Example: You look cold. Fancy a cuppa?

Usage: Informal British invitation; cuppa means a cup of tea.

title: We should catch up
description: We should share our recent news.
details:
Example: We should catch up over lunch.

Usage: Conversational; usually with someone you already know.

title: Make yourself at home
description: Feel relaxed and comfortable here.
details:
Example: Come in and make yourself at home.

Usage: Neutral; welcome a guest.

title: Help yourself
description: Take what you want without asking.
details:
Example: There’s cake on the table; help yourself.

Usage: Neutral; offer food or other available items.

title: It’s on me
description: I will pay for this.
details:
Example: Put your wallet away; it’s on me.

Usage: Informal; offer to cover the cost.

title: Let’s play it by ear
description: Let’s decide as circumstances develop.
details:
Example: Let’s play it by ear on Saturday.

Usage: Conversational; avoid a fixed plan.

title: I’ll take a rain check
description: I decline now but may accept later.
details:
Example: I’ll take a rain check on dinner.

Usage: Informal; suggest postponement, not a firm new date.

title: Give me a shout
description: Contact me when you need something.
details:
Example: Give me a shout when you arrive.

Usage: Informal British usage; no literal shouting needed.

title: We hit it off
description: We liked each other immediately.
details:
Example: We hit it off at the party.

Usage: Informal; describe a good first connection.

title: We go back a long way
description: We have known each other for years.
details:
Example: Sam and I go back a long way.

Usage: Conversational; a long-standing relationship.

title: We’ve drifted apart
description: We have gradually become less close.
details:
Example: We’ve drifted apart since school.

Usage: Neutral; gradual loss of closeness.

title: We see eye to eye
description: We agree with each other.
details:
Example: We see eye to eye on most things.

Usage: Conversational; often followed by on.

title: Clear the air
description: Discuss tension to improve a relationship.
details:
Example: Let’s clear the air before dinner.

Usage: Conversational; address an awkward disagreement.

title: No hard feelings
description: There is no lasting resentment.
details:
Example: You chose someone else? No hard feelings.

Usage: Conversational; reassure after disappointment or conflict.

title: I didn’t mean it like that
description: You misunderstood my intention.
details:
Example: Sorry, I didn’t mean it like that.

Usage: Conversational; clarify an unintended implication.

title: You can count on me
description: You can rely on my support.
details:
Example: You can count on me to help.

Usage: Neutral; a reassuring promise.

title: I owe you one
description: I will return your favour.
details:
Example: Thanks for the lift; I owe you one.

Usage: Informal; express gratitude for help.

title: Keep in touch
description: Continue contacting each other.
details:
Example: It was lovely meeting you; keep in touch.

Usage: Neutral; a friendly goodbye.

title: Send my regards
description: Pass on my polite good wishes.
details:
Example: Send my regards to your parents.

Usage: Neutral to formal; pass a greeting through someone.

title: I’ll leave you to it
description: I will let you continue undisturbed.
details:
Example: You’re busy, so I’ll leave you to it.

Usage: Conversational; politely end an interruption.
